accounting.rationale: R401 supplies a nonempty comma-separated list. The original explicit R1534 production governs dummy-arg-name and overrides the assumed R402 convention; R1539's unnamed alternate-return asterisk is not that name production.

Normative statement-to-INTENT route for the listed dummy arguments. Eligibility, IN/OUT/INOUT meaning, invocation state, definition/association contexts, allocation and finalization retain8.5.10, Clause15, Clause19 and their direct owners. No local S runtime effect or no-op classifier is created.
The separate R852 statement is one explicit route under8.5.1. It does not itself invoke a procedure, transfer data, allocate/deallocate an object or execute finalization.

R828 defines IN, OUT and INOUT. IN pointer association is distinct from permitted operations on its live definable target; OUT has entry-state and initialization qualifications, while INOUT and omitted INTENT are not equivalent.

C845 admits dummy data objects and dummy procedure pointers. A nonpointer dummy procedure is not eligible merely because its name is in the formal list. The name production does not supply POINTER, an actual dummy role or a missing interface.

PENDING exact8.5.10/15/19 source relations: preserve nonpointer definition restrictions, pointer association restrictions, OUT default-initialization and finalization/deallocation ordering, actual definability and always-defined zero-sized/zero-length objects. These are not a blanket old-value guarantee, an undefined read or a required trap. Existing INTENT/default-initialization/BIND/SAVE cases and C815's deletion control remain unchanged and are not automatically statement-effect witnesses.

The original subroutine prefix names A and B as formal arguments and gives both INOUT through a single INTENT statement. It is illustrative, not a complete executable program or an independent obligation.
SUBROUTINE EX is the containing procedure, not a module attribute declaration or a BLOCK specification.
Both listed names already occur as formal arguments in the shown header. A similarly spelled local entity would not be repaired by the INTENT statement alone.
INOUT is one intent-spec alternative under R828, with canonical actual-argument requirements. The fragment supplies no caller, value or update.
The optional double colon is present and one comma separates two distinct dummy names. It is not a per-name intent-spec or permission for a duplicate explicit attribute.

PENDING a completed ordinary subroutine with explicit supported data types when IMPLICIT NONE is used and a proper ending; any invocation also needs lawful actuals. No missing type/interface or undefined input is used as evidence for the statement.

requirements.title: An INTENT statement has a required parenthesized intent and a nonempty dummy-name list
requirements.source: 8.6.9 R852, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF139, printed125.
requirements.definition: INTENT is followed by a required parenthesized intent-spec, an optional double colon and a required nonempty comma-separated dummy-arg-name list. R828 owns the three intent-spec values; explicit R1534 owns the name production and R401 the list. Syntax does not make an arbitrary identifier an eligible dummy: C845 separately requires a dummy data object or dummy procedure pointer, not an ordinary nonpointer dummy procedure.

pending.parenthesized-intent-spec-forms: PENDING complete ordinary subroutines with genuine typed scalar INTEGER dummy x and separate INTENT(IN), INTENT(OUT) and INTENT(INOUT) statements. Keep the type declaration free of another INTENT specification and the body free of data/association use. These compile/positive-controls admit R852's form; R828 and8.5.10 own the chosen value and its meaning.
pending.optional-double-colon: PENDING equivalent complete contexts for INTENT(IN) :: x and INTENT(IN) x, with the same dummy header and type. The parentheses are required in both; optional double colons neither remove the name-list requirement nor legalize another intent-spec.
pending.multiple-distinct-dummy-names: PENDING a complete typed SUBROUTINE ex(a,b) with INTENT(INOUT) :: a,b, following the original note's roles. Both names occur once in the formal list and once in the statement; there is no prior type-declaration INTENT. If the procedure is later invoked, its actual arguments must meet the corresponding type/definability conditions rather than supplying an unrelated call failure.
pending.missing-parenthesized-specification: PENDING a complete data-dummy context with INTENT :: x, repaired only by adding (IN), and a separate missing-right-parenthesis contrast repaired by inserting that delimiter. Hold the dummy name, type, scope and all other syntax valid. Require the intended required intent-spec/group cause; a malformed procedure header, unknown INTENT word or generic EOF/missing-END report is not this isolated predicate.
pending.missing-dummy-name-list: PENDING complete subroutines whose specification part contains INTENT(IN) :: without a name and separately INTENT(IN) without a name. Add only the already declared formal dummy x for each repair. There is no listless all-dummies form; use no wrong-type, nondummy-role or duplicate-INTENT control.
pending.list-separator-repairs: PENDING complete typed two-dummy contexts with one missing comma between names or one trailing comma, repaired only at that separator. R401 supplies the nonempty comma-list convention. Repeating the same name is a C815 issue rather than a valid way to test list length or a substitute for the intended grammar error.
pending.name-not-designator-or-alternate-return: PENDING INTENT(IN) :: x(1) on an otherwise valid named array dummy, repaired by deleting only (1), and a separately qualified derived dummy obj%leaf contrast repaired to the whole eligible obj. R1534 requires a name, not a selected subobject. The unnamed alternate-return '*' allowed by R1539 is not a dummy-arg-name; do not invent a valid control that requires changing the procedure's dummy roles or ignores component/definition rules.
pending.data-and-procedure-pointer-role-source: PENDING a complete module with a prior abstract subroutine interface and a contained procedure whose callback formal is declared PROCEDURE(signature), POINTER, followed by a separate INTENT statement. The name has the real procedure-pointer role; no invocation or status inquiry is made. An ordinary nonpointer dummy procedure and a nondummy local are C845 contrasts, not R852 syntax errors. Data-pointer and procedure-pointer actual/interface rules in15.5.2.8/.10, and IN/OUT/INOUT differences, remain separate canonical gates.
pending.scope-order-and-duplicate-source: PENDING canonical C815,11.1.4C1107 and19.5.1.4 relations. An INTENT type-declaration attribute plus a statement on the same entity is duplication, not a valid statement control. C815_invalid:intent-stmt contains the second statement; C815_valid__c815_attribute_intent_stmt_control deletes it and is not an R852 witness. BLOCK forbids an INTENT statement, and naming a USE/host entity does not manufacture a local formal dummy. Keep complete local declarations, legitimate statement ordering and explicit interfaces where required, with no owner or role migration.
pending.canonical-intent-effect-and-state-source: PENDING exact8.5.10 and Clause15/19 mechanisms, without a local runtime classifier. Nonpointer IN forbids definition/undefinition; pointer IN constrains association rather than all target access. Nonpointer OUT has its qualified entry undefinition/default initialization, allocatable deallocation and finalization rules; pointer OUT has undefined association, not a prescribed false ASSOCIATED result.7.5.4.6p7/p8,7.5.6.3p7 and9.7.3.2p6 retain their full subject/order/elemental/C-interface premises. Zero-sized arrays and zero-length strings stay always defined under19.6.2 but that is not presence, allocation or association. Real state/effect parents need lawful actuals, defined-value/event oracles and exact completion; missing INTENT is not INOUT, undefined inputs are not read or trapped, and existing default-init/BIND/SAVE/finalization/intent cases are not cloned or retagged.

requirements.oracle: Complete compile/positive-controls for the actual statement grammar and source-isolated delimiter/list failures with minimal valid repairs. Dummy identity, procedure-pointer eligibility, intent semantics and state transitions retain their canonical owners. Any eventual reporting predicate must bind the specific grammar/role condition and legitimate live source origin after independent review and calibration.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All facets are pending. Required numbered reporting does not prescribe fatal status, English wording or printed R852. A bare INTENT/dummy/expected token, wrong role/type, repeated attribute, missing module/interface, unsupported feature, echo, quoted example, wrong-source recovery, Internal/ASR/verifier failure, crash or resource error cannot qualify. Statement acceptance is not invocation, argument transfer, allocation, initialization or finalization evidence. No compile-only substitute for mandatory canonical runtime effects, no undefined-value/status read and no universal runtime trap is invented.

review_rationale: Independent complete original INTENT statement source and plans reviewed in receipt12c752e5dd21c9e0273b130de1b3415bd8189f33bd4416440f9394b06c149ba9 and registered in doc/source_audits/batch_074.json. R852 requires a parenthesized R828 intent-spec and nonempty list; explicit R1534/C1571, not assumed R402 or alternate-return syntax, owns real dummy names. Actual data dummies and procedure-pointer dummies are eligible; an ordinary nonpointer dummy procedure is not. Pointer IN association restrictions differ from lawful operations on a live definable target; OUT default initialization/deallocation/finalization and undefined pointer status retain exact canonical conditions. No ASSOCIATED query of undefined status, payload read, no-op state classifier, guessed shape limit, clone of C815 controls or automatic numbered link is introduced. All new facets remain pending.
